title: Randomization as anisotropic noise
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $f$ be real-valued on its outcome space, and choose $r\in\{0,1\}^n$ and an outcome $x$. Set $s_i=1$ when $r_i=0$ and $s_i=-1$ when $r_i=1$. Then the randomized expansion at $r$ equals the anisotropic product noise with coordinate rates $s_i$, evaluated at $x$: $R_rf(x)=T_{\boldsymbol{s}}f(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is a real-valued function on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $r\in\{0,1\}^n$. For $s_i=(-1)^{r_i}$, $R_rf(x)=T_{\boldsymbol s}f(x)$ for every $x\in\Omega$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$; $R_rh=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\chi_S(r)h_S$; $T_{\boldsymbol s}h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}(\prod_{i\in S}s_i)h_S$ for real coordinate rates $s_i$.
